plain_rule_summary: A tenant-landlord issue usually depends on the rental agreement, possession status, rent payment, notice, and applicable state law.
If the agreement period is still active, the termination clause and notice terms become important.
Forceful eviction, lockout, threats, or removal of belongings should be treated as urgent legal-risk facts.
The system should not conclude whether eviction is valid; it should explain what facts and documents matter.
important_documents: photos/videos of lockout or force if any
common_missing_facts: Is the rental agreement written or oral?
What is the start date and end date of the agreement?
Has the landlord given written notice?
Is there any unpaid rent or breach alleged?
Has there been threat, force, lockout, police pressure, or removal of goods?
Which city/state is the property located in?
Is the property residential or commercial?
possible_rights: Possible right to rely on the rental agreement terms.
Possible right to receive proper notice where required.
Possible protection against forceful dispossession or illegal lockout.
Possible right to preserve possession until lawful procedure is followed, depending on facts and local law.
possible_remedies: Review the termination and notice clauses in the rental agreement.
Preserve rent receipts, agreement copy, notices, messages, and payment records.
Ask the landlord to communicate in writing.
Avoid verbal-only settlement if there is pressure or threat.
Consult a qualified local lawyer urgently if there is force, lockout, police involvement, or immediate dispossession risk.
possible_outcomes: If the landlord has not followed notice or agreed termination terms, the eviction attempt may be contestable.
If there is rent default or breach, the landlord may have stronger grounds depending on law and facts.
If force or lockout is used, urgent legal help may be required.
The outcome depends on agreement terms, local tenancy law, evidence, and possession facts.
response_guidance: Do not say the tenant will win or landlord will lose.
Do not give a final legal opinion.
Ask missing questions about notice, rent default, agreement terms, and state.
Trigger lawyer warning if force, lockout, threat, court notice, or police is involved.
